title: Health and Well-being
description: Ten short stories about health and well-being: a visit to the doctor, sleeping well, walking, running, eating well and staying strong.

lessons.title: Sam's Shot
lessons.summary: Linda takes her baby, Sam, to the health center for a shot.
lessons.text:
Linda was a young mother. She had a baby boy named Sam. Sam was 6 months old.

Every few months, a baby needs a visit to the doctor. This month, Sam needed a visit, and he needed a shot. A shot helps a baby stay strong.

Linda called the health center. "Is the doctor available this week?" she asked. "No, she isn't available this week," said the woman on the phone. "But she is available next week, at 10 in the morning."

The next week, Linda got Sam ready. She put him in the car, and they drove to the health center. They got there 10 minutes early. They waited in the front room with other mothers and their babies. After 15 minutes, the doctor came out and called his name.

First, the doctor looked at Sam. She checked his eyes and his heart. "He is a strong baby," she said. "Now he is ready for his shot."

Linda held Sam close. The shot took only a second. Sam did not like it, but after a few minutes he was happy again.

"It wasn't so bad," Linda said to him. "You were very good."

"See you at his next visit in 3 months," said the doctor. Then Linda and Sam went home.

Questions:
Who was Linda?
Linda was a young mother.
How old was Sam?
Sam was 6 months old.
What did Sam need this month?
This month, he needed a shot.
When was the doctor available?
The doctor was available the next week, at 10 in the morning.
Where did Linda and Sam wait?
They waited in the front room for 15 minutes.
Was the shot bad for Sam?
No, it wasn't so bad. After a few minutes, he was happy again.
When is Sam's next visit?
His next visit is in 3 months.

lessons.title: The Police Test
lessons.summary: Mike, a police officer, makes a plan to get stronger and passes his yearly test.
lessons.text:
Mike was a police officer. He worked for the police department in a big city. Every year, each officer in the department had to pass a test. The test showed that the officers were strong and fast.

This year, Mike had a problem. He was 45 years old, and he wasn't as fast as before. "I need to be stronger and faster," he said. He had a goal. He wanted to pass the test in six weeks. This was his only chance this year.

So Mike made a plan with 3 steps. Step one: he walked to work every day. Step two: he ran after work 3 times a week. Step three: he went up and down the steps of his building 20 times every night.

At first, it was very hard. Mike ran for 10 minutes, and then he had to stop. But every week, he ran a little further. In week 2, he ran for 15 minutes. In week 4, he ran for 25 minutes. He also ate good food and drank a lot of water.

After six weeks, the day of the test came. Mike was ready. He ran fast, and he went up the steps fast. He completed every part of the test. He reached his goal!

"Good job, Mike," said the head of the department. "You are one of the strongest officers here." Mike was very happy. He wanted to keep his plan. "Next year, I will have another chance to do even better," he said.

Questions:
What was Mike's job?
Mike was a police officer.
What was his goal?
His goal was to pass the test in six weeks.
What was step one of his plan?
Step one was to walk to work every day.
How far did Mike run every week?
He ran a little further every week.
Did Mike complete the test?
Yes. He completed every part of the test and reached his goal.

lessons.title: No Phone at Night
lessons.summary: Emma sleeps badly because of her phone, puts it in another room and sleeps well again.
lessons.text:
Emma had a problem: she could not sleep well. Every morning she felt bad, and all day she wanted to rest.

At night, Emma always looked at her phone. She read page after page on social media. She opened link after link. Sometimes she watched a whole movie on her phone. When she put the phone down, it was often 2 in the morning.

One day, Emma talked to her friend Lily. Lily said, "Your phone has a bad effect on your sleep. The light from the phone tells your body that it is still day. And a loss of sleep is bad for your body and your mind."

So Emma tried something new. At 10 every night, she put her phone in the living room. The phone remained there all night. In her room, she read a real book rather than the news on her phone. She also turned on a small fan, because she liked the sound of the fan.

The first night was hard. Emma wanted to read just one more page and watch just one more movie. But the phone remained in the living room.

After a week, Emma went to sleep at 11 every night. She got 8 hours of rest. In the morning she felt great. The effect was easy to see: no phone at night meant better sleep.

Questions:
What did Emma do on her phone at night?
She read page after page on social media and watched movies.
What did Lily say about the phone?
She said the phone has a bad effect on sleep, and a loss of sleep is bad for your body and your mind.
Where did the phone remain at night?
The phone remained in the living room.
What did Emma read rather than the news on her phone?
She read a real book.
How did Emma feel after a week?
She felt great after 8 hours of rest.

lessons.title: Frank and Max
lessons.summary: Frank, who does not like walking, gets a young dog and starts to walk every day.
lessons.text:
Frank was 70 years old. He lived by himself in a small town. Every day he stayed at home and watched television. He did not move much, and his body did not feel strong.

The doctor told him, "You need to walk every day." But Frank did not enjoy walking. "I don't enjoy it," he said. "I have no reason to go out."

One day, his son Steve came to visit. He brought a young dog. "This is Max," said Steve. "He needs a home, and he needs to walk every day too."

Now Frank had a reason to go out. Every morning, Frank and Max walked to the big park on the west side of town. Frank always wore his old watch, so he knew how long they walked. He carried water for himself and for Max. Sometimes Max ran in front of Frank. Sometimes he stayed behind Frank and stopped to look at something. Then Frank waited for him.

In the park, there were many other people with dogs. Among them, Frank found new friends. They walked together and talked about their dogs. Sometimes one of them carried food for all the dogs.

After a month, Frank walked for an hour every day. His body felt strong again. "I enjoy our walks now," he told Steve. "Max is my best friend."

Questions:
Where did Frank live?
He lived in a small town.
Who brought Max?
His son Steve brought Max.
Where did Frank and Max walk every morning?
They walked to the big park on the west side of town.
What did Frank always wear?
He always wore his old watch.
What did Max sometimes do?
Sometimes he ran in front of Frank, and sometimes he stayed behind him.
What did Frank carry?
He carried water for himself and for Max.
What did Frank find among the people in the park?
He found new friends among them.

lessons.title: The Running Club
lessons.summary: Kate, a college student, joins the running club and comes to love running.
lessons.text:
Kate was a student at a college in a big city. She studied all day and did not move much. She wanted to change that.

One day in March, Kate saw a sign on a board in front of the student center. The sign said: "Running Club. We meet 3 times a week. All students can join." Kate had an interest in running, so she joined the club.

The head of the club was Paul. He was a former student at the college. He said, "Running is a part of a good education. A strong body helps a strong mind."

In the club, the students could choose a short run or a long run. In the first week, Kate chose the short run. It was not easy, but she enjoyed it. After a few weeks, she chose the long run.

The club grew fast. In March, there were 10 students. A month later, there were 20. Two months later, there were 30. Every month, Paul put the names of the fastest students on the board. Kate wanted to see her name there.

At the end of the year, the club had a major event: a long run through the city. Kate completed it, and her name was on the board. Her interest in running grew and grew. Now running is a major part of her life.

Questions:
Where did Kate see the sign?
She saw the sign on a board in front of the student center.
Who was Paul?
He was the head of the club and a former student at the college.
What did Paul say about running?
He said running is a part of a good education.
How fast did the club grow?
It grew fast. In March, there were 10 students. Two months later, there were 30.
What was the major event at the end of the year?
It was a long run through the city.

lessons.title: Reading the Back
lessons.summary: Amy learns to read the figures on the back of food products and changes what she buys.
lessons.text:
Amy wanted to eat better. But she had one main problem. She did not know whether a food was good or bad for her.

One day at the market, Amy picked up a product and looked at the back. There was a list with a lot of figures on it. The figures were not clear to her. She did not know whether a big number was good or bad.

At home, Amy learned the main things to look for. After that, the figures were clear.

The next week, Amy went back to the market. She looked at the back of every product. Some products were good value for the money, but they had a lot of sugar. Good value was not enough. Others were much better for her body. She made a list of products and put a mark next to each good one.

Amy also made a plan. Every week, she traded one bad product for a better one. In week 1, she traded her sweet drink for water. In week 2, she traded a sweet food for a food with less sugar. After that, she did not want either of the old products.

Today, Amy's current list has a mark next to almost every product. She feels great, and the reason is clear.

Questions:
What was Amy's main problem?
She did not know whether a food was good or bad for her.
What was on the back of the product?
There was a list with a lot of figures on it.
What did Amy put next to each good product?
She put a mark next to each good product.
What did Amy trade in week 1?
She traded her sweet drink for water.
Did Amy want either of the old products after that?
No, she did not want either of them.
What is on Amy's current list?
There is a mark next to almost every product.

lessons.title: Two Brothers
lessons.summary: Ben has a heart problem, and his brother Jack helps him walk every day.
lessons.text:
Jack and Ben were brothers. Jack was 50, and his brother Ben was 55. They lived in the same city.

One day, Ben called Jack. "I don't feel well," he said. Jack drove to Ben's house and took him to the health center. He dropped Ben off at the front door.

The doctor checked Ben's heart. "Your heart is not quite right," she said. "It isn't a big problem yet. But you need to walk every day, and you need to eat better."

Ben did not listen. He went home and did nothing. A couple of weeks later, Jack heard about it from Ben's son. Jack went to see his brother. "You need to listen to the doctor," Jack said.

"I know," said Ben. "But I can't do it by myself. I wish I were stronger."

"Then I will walk with you," said Jack. "I need it too. I can't do it by myself either." Ben agreed.

Every morning, Jack came to Ben's house, and they walked for 30 minutes. At first, it was quite hard for Ben. After a couple of weeks, it was easier. They talked about their kids and about old times.

After 3 months, Jack drove Ben to the health center again and dropped him off at the door. The doctor checked his heart. "You're fine now," she said. "You listened to me." Ben was happy. "I listened to my brother too," he said.

Questions:
How old were the brothers?
Jack was 50, and Ben was 55.
What did the doctor tell Ben?
She said he needed to walk every day and eat better.
How did Jack hear about it?
He heard about it from Ben's son.
What did Ben wish?
He said, "I wish I were stronger."
Did Ben agree to walk with Jack?
Yes, Ben agreed.
What did the doctor say after 3 months?
She said, "You're fine now."

lessons.title: Rosa's Back
lessons.summary: Rosa builds car parts all day, has back problems and gets better with the doctor's help.
lessons.text:
Rosa worked in the car industry. She worked in a big building where people build cars. Her job was to build small car parts. Every day, she stood for 8 hours.

Then one day, Rosa's back started to give her problems. Every night, her back felt bad. So she went to the health center.

The doctor showed her a model of the back. "Look at this model," she said. "There is a little space between these parts. When you stand the wrong way all day, there is less space here. That is bad for your back."

According to the doctor, Rosa needed to do 3 things: stand the right way, take short breaks and move her back every morning. "Your company must allow you to take short breaks," she said. "I can send them a note today." Rosa asked her to send it.

The company read the note and agreed to allow Rosa a break of 5 minutes every hour.

A week later, Rosa got a bill from the health center. The health center charged $80 for the visit, but her company paid half of the bill.

Although it was hard at first, Rosa moved her back every morning. Although her job is still hard, her back is much better now.

Questions:
Where did Rosa work?
She worked in the car industry.
What did the doctor show Rosa?
She showed her a model of the back.
According to the doctor, what did Rosa need to do?
She needed to stand the right way, take short breaks and move her back every morning.
What did the doctor want to send to the company?
She wanted to send them a note.
What did the company allow Rosa to take?
It agreed to allow her a break of 5 minutes every hour.
How much did the health center charge for the visit?
It charged $80, and her company paid half of the bill.

lessons.title: Walking Together
lessons.summary: Tom, a city official, and his wife join one of the city's new free walking groups.
lessons.text:
Tom was a city official. He worked in a big office in the center of the city. He was in meetings or on the phone most of the day.

Last year, the city started a new policy. The policy was about the health of the people in the city. With money from a city fund, the city started free walking groups in every park. Each group met 3 times a week.

Tom worked on the new policy, but at first he did not join a group himself. "I don't have time," he said. Then one night, his wife Ann asked him, "Why don't we join a group together?" Tom said yes.

The program ran for a period of 6 months. Tom and his wife walked with their group 3 times a week. They talked a lot on their walks. It was good for their health. It was also good for their relationship. "We talk more now," Ann said. "Our relationship is better than before."

At the end of the period, the city did a review of the policy. Tom read the review. More than 5,000 people walked in the groups, and most of them felt better. The review said the policy worked well, so the city put more money into the fund.

Tom will never forget those 6 months. He and his wife still walk with their group today. "Don't forget your water," Ann tells him before every walk.

Questions:
What was Tom's job?
Tom was a city official.
What was the new policy about?
It was about the health of the people in the city.
Where did the money for the groups come from?
It came from a city fund.
How long was the period of the program?
It was a period of 6 months.
What did Ann say about their relationship?
She said their relationship was better than before.
What did the review say?
The review said the policy worked well.

lessons.title: Leo Learns Tennis
lessons.summary: Leo plays video games all day until his father teaches him tennis in the park.
lessons.text:
Leo was 11 years old. He loved video games. After school, he played the same game for hours. In the game, his character was very fast and very strong. But Leo himself did not move at all.

Leo's parents did not like this. "Games are fine sometimes," said his father, Dan. "But you need to move your body too." Leo's mother agreed with his father.

One day, Dan had an idea. "Do you want to learn tennis?" he asked Leo. "It's a lot of fun." Leo was not sure, but he said yes.

The next day, Dan took Leo to the park. First, Dan showed Leo how to serve. Leo tried to serve again and again. His first 20 serves were bad. But then he served well, and his father said, "Great serve!" Leo was happy. This was fun.

Leo and his father played in the park every day for a couple of weeks. Then they played their first real match. Dan won the match, but Leo did not care. The match was a lot of fun.

That night, Leo did not play his video game. He drew a picture of himself and his father in the park. In the picture, Leo was the main character, not the character from his game. His parents were happy, and they put the drawing on the wall.

Questions:
What did Leo do after school?
He played the same video game for hours.
What did Leo's father say?
He said, "Games are fine sometimes, but you need to move your body too."
What did Dan show Leo in the park?
He showed Leo how to serve.
Who won the first match?
Dan won the match, but Leo had fun.
What did Leo draw?
He drew a picture of himself and his father in the park.
What did Leo's parents do with the drawing?
They put the drawing on the wall.
